ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in Figure A, three identical horseshoe magnets are placed side by side on a horizontal table, and the magnetic field between the poles can be considered uniform. A straight conductor rod is horizontally suspended between the poles of the magnets, with the rod perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic induction. The gravitational force on the conductor rod is $G$, and the effective length of the rod in the uniform magnetic field is $L$. When a current $I$ passes through the conductor rod, the rod deflects outward (but remains between the poles), and at rest, the angle between the suspension line and the vertical direction is $\theta$. The force diagram on the cross-section of the conductor rod at this moment is shown in Figure B, where the Ampere force $F$ is directed horizontally to the right.

1. What is the magnitude of the Ampere force $F$ acting on the conductor rod?
2. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B$ of this uniform magnetic field?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure A, three identical horseshoe magnets are placed side by side on a horizontal table, and the magnetic field between the poles can be considered uniform. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure A, three identical horseshoe-shaped magnets can be seen placed side by side, and a straight conducting rod passes horizontally through between the magnetic poles; Figure B is a force diagram of the cross section of the conducting rod, the rod is subjected to the tension F_T along the direction of the suspension line, the vertically downward gravity G, and the horizontally rightward Ampere force F, and the angle between the suspension line and the vertical dashed line is labeled θ. Reasoning: The conducting rod is at rest, so the forces are balanced. Decompose the suspension-line tension F_T into a vertical component and a horizontal component. Balance in the vertical direction: F_T cosθ = G. Balance in the horizontal direction: F_T sinθ = F. Dividing the two equations gives F/G = tanθ, therefore the magnitude of the Ampere force F = G tanθ. Also because the conducting rod is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic induction intensity, its effective length in the uniform magnetic field is L, and the current passing through it is I, so the Ampere force F = BIL. Thus B = F/(IL) = G tanθ/(IL).
